scope.goal: Determine everything needed to run DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (GGUF) on Zeus's 4x Intel Arc Pro B70 (128 GB total VRAM, Windows 25H2), and produce a minimal, source-backed port plan with acceptance checks.
constraints: Research-only: no builds, no execution, no live-service changes (llama-swap and Zeus runtime untouched)
GPUs sit on the Windows side of Zeus; the target path is Windows-native, not WSL2/Docker
Budget: 128 GB VRAM (4x32 GB) plus ~100 GB usable of 112 GB system RAM
llama.cpp master checkout already exists at D:\llama-unmap2; oneAPI 2026.0/2025.1 already installed
non_goals: Actually downloading, building or running the model on Zeus in this run
Distilled/smaller variants as the primary deliverable (Maya-XS is fallback only)
Posting anything to upstream repos (llama.cpp bans agent-written text)
Non-GGUF stacks (MLX, safetensors-only) as the primary path

limitations: Performance anchors are for smaller models, not the full 1017 on B70s
4-card Windows layer split is not publicly documented as stable; all public B70 SYCL reports are Linux
Exact KV cache size for V4.1 compressed KV at 32-64K context is not documented in inspected sources
The b12445 win-sycl zip contents were not unpacked; asset list observed only

questions.question: Does llama.cpp support loading DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 GGUFs on the SYCL backend, and from which release?
questions.resolution: Yes. PR #31086 (model: DSV4.1 flash) merged 2026-10-25, so releases >= b11870 load V4.1 GGUFs; the latest release b12445 (published 2026-11-16T20:44Z) ships a prebuilt win-sycl zip.

questions.question: Which GGUF quant of the full 1017 model fits Zeus's 128 GB VRAM + ~100 GB usable RAM?
questions.resolution: Only unsloth UD-IQ1_S (233 GB) is in budget, and only with partial CPU offload; official ggml-org quants start at Q2_K_S (~298 GB) and do not fit. The engram table is swappable to smaller quants via set_split.py to reclaim budget.

questions.question: Are there known B70/Xe2 SYCL bugs that would block V4.1 flash on Arc?
questions.resolution: One known blocker - issue #26462, a SIGSEGV in the SYCL set_rows kernel on Arc from a missing f16->bf16 conversion - is fixed; the fix was verified present at the pinned local master commit and at tag b12445.

questions.question: How is a 4-GPU configuration done with SYCL on Windows, and how well is it proven?
questions.resolution: Documented mechanism: ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR='level_zero:*' (or an explicit per-device list) + ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=1 (docs-recommended for layer mode) + --split-mode layer. Docs note tensor split is optimized for 2 GPUs (other counts fall back to a generic all-reduce); all public B70 SYCL field reports are Linux, so 4-card Windows layer-split stability is an accepted risk with fallbacks (2+2 card pairs or 2-GPU tensor mode).

questions.question: What performance should be expected for the full 1017 on 4x B70?
questions.resolution: No published number for the full 1017 on B70-class hardware. Anchors: Maya-XS distilled on 88 GB Arc (Linux): 45.6 t/s prefill, 10.9 t/s decode @64K; snailium smaller model on B70 (Docker/Linux): 470-490 t/s prefill, 41-46 t/s decode. Expect single-digit to low-double-digit decode t/s for the full 1017 with CPU-offloaded experts/engram; measure, don't assume.

decisions.candidate: llama.cpp SYCL backend, Windows-native, prebuilt win-sycl b12445 (source build from D:\llama-unmap2 via examples\sycl\win-build-sycl.bat as fallback)
decisions.rationale: Only path with (a) DSV4.1-Flash model support in current releases, (b) a Windows SYCL prebuilt that needs no oneAPI at runtime, (c) documented multi-GPU configuration, (d) the known B70 crash fixed, and (e) a field report of V4.1 GGUFs running on Arc.
decisions.complexity_cost: Low: download, two env vars, a few flags; no compilation unless the prebuilt fails.
decisions.scale_fit: Built for exactly this: single-machine local inference with multi-card Level Zero devices.
decisions.revisit_trigger: If the prebuilt b12445 zip fails to enumerate all 4 cards or crashes, fall back to a source build of D:\llama-unmap2 with win-build-sycl.bat (same backend, oneAPI already installed).

decisions.candidate: unsloth UD-IQ1_S full quant (~233 GB) with swappable engram table (start with bundled default; swap to IQ4_NL 110.6 GB via set_split.py if RAM is tight)
decisions.rationale: The only full quant below the usable budget; the engram swap is a documented knob that can recover tens of GB if the default engram quant is large.
decisions.complexity_cost: Low: one ~233 GB download plus one optional engram-swap step.
decisions.scale_fit: 233 GB against a ~224 GB usable budget forces partial offload; quality is the floor of available full quants.
decisions.revisit_trigger: If UD-IQ1_S quality is unacceptable or the fit fails after engram swap, move to a smaller engram quant, a smaller context, or the distilled variant.

decisions.candidate: 4x B70 with --split-mode layer, ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR='level_zero:*', ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=1 (docs-recommended for layer mode), q8_0 KV cache, 32K starting context, maximum GPU offload
decisions.rationale: The documented multi-GPU configuration; q8_0 KV keeps the 32K cache small; 32K is a starting point chosen against the tight KV budget, not a ceiling.
alternatives: Single B70 (32 GB - insufficient for any full quant)
2-GPU tensor split (docs' optimized case, but halves VRAM capacity)
decisions.complexity_cost: Low: flags and env vars only.
decisions.scale_fit: 128 GB across 4 cards is the only way to hold most of a 233 GB model in GPU memory.
decisions.revisit_trigger: If the 4-card layer split is unstable (crash, lopsided load), try 2+2 card pairs (two independent 2-GPU servers) or --split-mode tensor (documented 2-GPU-optimized tensor mode, requires flash attention); if 32K KV does not fit, drop to 16K.

decisions.candidate: vLLM with the XPU (Intel GPU) backend
decisions.rationale: No DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash GGUF support found in the inspected vLLM-XPU path, and no per-tensor CPU offload / engram swap equivalent; every inspected field report of V4.1 on Arc is llama.cpp SYCL.
decisions.complexity_cost: Higher: XPU plugin stack, safetensors conversion, no GGUF path.
decisions.scale_fit: Aimed at datacenter XPU servers; 4-card pro-Arc consumer-class multi-GPU is a second-order case.
decisions.revisit_trigger: If vLLM-XPU lands DSV4.1-Flash plus MoE CPU offload on Arc and higher throughput is needed.

decisions.rationale: EXL3 targets CUDA GPUs; no Intel SYCL/Level Zero backend was found in the inspected version, so it cannot run on the B70s at all.
decisions.revisit_trigger: An EXL3 Intel backend appears that supports DSV4.1-Flash.

decisions.candidate: WSL2/Docker Linux SYCL route (snailium B70 image)
decisions.rationale: The GPUs sit on the Windows side; 4-card Arc visibility through WSL2 is not publicly verified, Docker Desktop is currently stopped, and the Windows-native path is documented and one layer closer to the hardware. The snailium config remains useful as a tuning reference (flags), which is why it stays in the ledger.
decisions.complexity_cost: Medium: WSL2 GPU setup, 4-card visibility, ~343 GB of downloads inside WSL.
decisions.scale_fit: Proven on single B70-class cards in Docker; 4-card unverified.
decisions.revisit_trigger: If the Windows-native 4-card layer split proves unstable and WSL2 shows all 4 cards with ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=1.

decisions.candidate: ggml-org Q2_K_S (~298 GB) / Q2_K (~335 GB) as the primary quant
decisions.rationale: 298-335 GB exceeds the ~224 GB usable budget even with maximal CPU offload; higher quality than UD-IQ1_S but it does not fit this machine.
decisions.scale_fit: Wrong size class for this machine.
decisions.revisit_trigger: More VRAM (e.g. an 8-card build) or a smaller active-footprint configuration that makes Q2_K_S viable.

decisions.rationale: Fits in 2-3 of the 4 cards with a published speed (10.9 t/s decode @64K), but it is a distilled model, not the full 1017 the user asked for; keep as fallback if UD-IQ1_S proves too slow or too weak.
decisions.scale_fit: Sized for exactly this class of hardware.
decisions.revisit_trigger: Measured decode on the full 1017 below ~5 t/s, or the user accepts a distilled model for speed.
